# arin_aspa (Resource)

Manage one hosted ASPA and its complete provider-AS set. The customer ASN must belong to the organization and be eligible for hosted RPKI. Import an existing ASPA first. Provider changes use one atomic delete/add transaction; unrelated ASPAs and ROAs are preserved. Destroy removes only this ASPA. ARIN rejects reserved provider ASNs except AS0 as the sole provider.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Use an ASN held by your organization and its actual provider ASNs.
# Import first if the ASPA already exists. Provider changes are atomic.
resource "arin_aspa" "example" {
  org_handle    = "EXAMPLE-1"
  customer_asn  = 19814
  provider_asns = [13335, 15169]
}

# An ASN with no providers can use provider_asns = [0].
# AS0 cannot be combined with other provider ASNs.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `customer_asn` (Number) Customer AS number owned by the organization. Changes require replacement.
- `org_handle` (String) Existing organization handle. Changes require replacement.
- `provider_asns` (Set of Number) Complete nonempty set of provider AS numbers. Must exclude the customer ASN. Use [0] to declare no providers; AS0 cannot be mixed with other ASNs.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ORG-HANDLE/CUSTOMER-ASN.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import arin_aspa.example EXAMPLE-1/19814
```
